Inside the U-Net

The notebook's segmentation network, stage by stage, with real feature maps for a test photo. The encoder (Lecture 15's ResNet-18) goes down the left side and the decoder comes up the right. Click a stage to see its shape and four of its channels. Then switch the skip connections off: that is a second network, trained the same way without them.

Test photo

Skip connections

Two separately trained networks. They share the architecture of the encoder and of the decoder, and differ only in whether the decoder also receives the encoder's feature maps.

Down: less where, more what
Click down the encoder. At 128 × 128 the maps are edge and texture pictures of the photo. At 8 × 8 a map is a few bright cells: the network knows roughly where the people are and nothing about their outline. The channel count grows as the size shrinks.

    
Up without skips: guessing the edges
Switch the skips off and click up the decoder. Every map is grown from the 8 × 8 bottleneck: a vague silhouette built from the repeating pattern of the transposed convolutions. The decoder has to invent the outline, because nothing it receives contains it.

    
Up with skips: edges handed across
With the skips on, each decoder stage also gets the encoder's maps of the same size. The decoder's maps become sharp at once, and the outline of the final mask follows the body. The cost is wider 3 × 3 convolutions: compare the parameter counts.
